sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Wilson County?
sections.html:
The Wilson County Tax Administration office lists, values and collects property tax for the county. It also collects for nine municipalities, two solid waste taxes, two special districts and fifteen fire districts, according to the county's tax administration page, so one bill can carry several layers.

Its counter sits at 113 Nash Street East in the city of Wilson, and its page lists four ways to pay, online among them. Bills go out by mail in early August, and from 2026 owners of residential dwellings outside a municipality receive a solid waste permit with that bill.

Mail is processed by the USPS postmark. The county warns that a drop box or a small post office may not stamp the same day, so send payments, listing forms and appeals several days early or ask the counter clerk for a postmark.

sections.h2: What should a Wilson County seller know about the local housing stock?
sections.html:
Roughly 373 square miles east of Raleigh make up the county. Its seat, the city of Wilson, holds more than 50,000 residents and about 14.2 square miles, per the county's own tax page. The county carries roughly 43,000 parcels in its real estate listing system.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table reports these county figures:

  • A 2025 estimate of 81,150 people, a 2.4% rise since the 2020 count.
  • 38,463 housing units, with owners living in 60.0% of occupied homes.
  • Typical owned homes valued at $186,000 and typical rent of $953.
  • Middle household income of $56,423 and a 22.5 minute average commute.

Six in ten occupied homes have owner residents.

sections.h2: What is the Wilson County payment deadline?
sections.html:
Bills fall due September 1. The county's published cutoff is January 6, and balances left after it are delinquent. Under G.S. 105-360, payment at face amount works up to the day before January 6.

Late interest begins at 2% for the first weeks and then climbs by three-fourths of a percent each month. Ask the tax office whether any early-payment discount applies, since a county may adopt a discount schedule by a resolution passed before May 1.

The county's FAQ answers a common seller question. The person on the deed as of January 1 receives the bill, and a later sale usually changes the name only for the following year.

sections.h2: How does the Wilson County revaluation affect an assessment?
sections.html:
Wilson County reappraised real property as of January 1, 2024, its first reappraisal since 2016, and the county's tax bill FAQ says it sits on a cycle of eight years. North Carolina law requires counties to reappraise at least that often.

The county told owners that its revaluation covered more than 41,000 real property parcels. It also split personal property onto its own bill, apart from real estate, beginning with the 2024 bills.

The county's Comper tool lets an owner compare a house with neighborhood sales as of the revaluation date. Those sales are the best evidence to bring to the tax office if a value looks high.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Wilson County value?
sections.html:
Get the current form and cutoff from the tax office. After the 2024 revaluation, the real property window closed May 16, 2024, when the review board adjourned, and a new one opened in January 2025.

State law sets the outer frame: the commissioners normally sit as the review board in spring (G.S. 105-322), and a loser at that stage has a month to go on to the state commission (G.S. 105-290).

For personal property, the county set a 2024 appeal cutoff of September 10 at 11:59 pm, and the appeal had to be in writing, by email or postmarked by then.

sections.h2: Which Wilson County owners can get tax relief?
sections.html:
Three state relief programs exist, and one owner draws on only one of them. The county tax office takes the application, and the state AV-9 form names June 1 as the cutoff.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shelters the larger of $25,000 or half a home's appraised value for older or fully disabled owners under the income ceiling, printed by NCDOR as $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes $45,000 of value for qualifying veterans, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: holds the bill to 4% or 5% of income, with the $58,200 ceiling, and defers the rest as a lien.

The rules are in G.S. 105-277.1 and on the NCDOR form.

sections.h2: What else can appear on a Wilson County tax bill?
sections.html:
Besides the county levy, a parcel may carry a municipal tax, a fire district tax, a special district tax or a solid waste charge, because the county collects for all of them. Which ones apply depends on where the house stands, so read the bill line by line.

Since 2024 the county has split personal property from real estate, which means a seller with a vehicle, boat or business equipment may receive two separate bills. For homes outside a municipality, the new solid waste permit arrives with the annual bill, so a buyer taking over such a house should ask the seller to hand it over at closing.

A house inside the city of Wilson is billed for city tax through the same office, and the tax calculator on the county site lets owners test the combined result with their assessed value.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell a Wilson County house with tax unpaid?
sections.html:
A balance follows the parcel into the sale, so closing is the moment to clear it. The lien arises on the listing date each year (G.S. 105-355), and collection can end in a court-supervised sale.

Wilson County adds a local step. Under G.S. 161-31 and a 2004 commissioners' resolution, the Register of Deeds takes a deed for recording only if it carries a statement about delinquent taxes. An attorney can complete the statement personally, or the deed goes first to the Collections Division of the tax department, where a clerk checks the parcel for delinquent tax. The county asks that taxes and recording fees go in separate checks. Questions go to the tax office at 252-399-2900, option 2.

sections.html:

faqs.q: How can I send a payment to the Wilson County tax office?
faqs.a: Visit the counter at 113 Nash Street East in Wilson, or use the county's online payment site. The tax administration page lists four methods in all.

faqs.q: Who receives the bill if I sell during the year?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner. The county's FAQ says a mid-year sale normally shows up the next tax year, so buyer and seller settle the split at closing.

faqs.q: Is the Wilson County cutoff January 5 or January 6?
faqs.a: The county's FAQ names January 6 as the last day, and state law allows par payment before January 6. Confirm the exact cutoff with the tax office before you pay late in the season.

faqs.q: Is a Wilson County appeal still open to me?
faqs.a: Ask the tax office, because the window depends on the year. The 2024 revaluation appeals closed May 16, 2024, and the following window opened in January 2025.

faqs.q: Do I need a clearance before recording a deed in Wilson County?
faqs.a: Yes, in the sense that the deed needs a delinquent tax statement. An attorney can sign it, or a tax department clerk can verify the parcel first, and the Register of Deeds then records it.
